newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht roars to 14-yr high but bourse plunges.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht roars to 14-yr high but bourse plunges.

text.p: A foreign scramble for Thai baht drove the currency to a new 14-year high in the offshore market on Tuesday, while the Thai bourse tumbled to a new 98-month low on weak bank stocks, dealers said.

Strong demand for the baht as investors tried to cover short positions sustained after the last speculative attack on the currency in mid-May saw it quoted at a new high of 22.800/000 against the dollar late in the offshore currency market, forex dealers said.
Bank stocks, meanwhile, were hit by worries that problems with non-performing loans problems may be worse than previously anticipated, brokers said.

The Thai stock index plummeted below the key 500-point level and ended the day off 13.83 points at 497.72. Analysts said it was hard to predict when it would reach bottom given its prolonged slide since mid-1996.

The baht has been trading in a two-tier market -- one offshore and the other onshore -- after the Bank of Thailand introduced currency controls last month and cut off local sources of baht supply to foreign speculators.
Thailand's central bank is determined to institutionalise the controls to ward off and punish baht speculators.

The controls have forced the offshore baht rate higher than the onshore rate as foreign speculators in need of baht after last month's short sales sold dollars heavily to buy the Thai unit to offset outstanding positions, dealers said.
In the onshore market the baht was quoted weaker at 25.820 against the dollar.

"Some foreign players have been caught by the central bank controls and we expect this squeeze to last for some months. At this rate hitting 22.00 baht to the dollar may be likely," said the treasurer of one foreign bank in Bangkok.
On the bourse, in addition to worries about bank profits, foreigners also dumped bank stocks on the foreign board of the Thai stock market apparently to raise baht funds, said brokers.
They added that traditional hefty price premiums fetched by major banks on the foreign board had fallen sharply during the past few sessions because of selling to raise baht.
On the main Thai stock exchange board, Bangkok Bank lost 10 baht to 122, Thai Farmers shed 6.00 to 83.50, and Siam Commercial Bank fell 3.50 to 94.50.

"The bear run is likely to continue for the rest of this week. It's hard to say where the bottom will be as today the strong key support of 500 was broken," said one broker at Nava Finance and Securities.
The lower profit expectations for banks were due to anticipation that the troubled finance sector's non-performing loans to mainly the depressed property sector would rise.
Thailand's economy has braked sharply since last year and the authorities expect growth this year to slow to a more than 10-year low of 5.9 percent against 6.4 percent posted in 1996.
Private economists have lowered their growth forecasts to between three and five percent for this year.
Among Thailand's key economic woes are a sharp slow down in exports, high interest rates that have stifled businesses and sluggish consumer and investment spending.
